items.title: Chubby Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: it’s a blues — so there’s three twelve bar phrases with the band and Pete Candoli’s gleaming, and I’m playing [scats].

ctx.x: Well it was shortly after that that I just graduated high school, so I went out to Ohio State in Columbus, Ohio. And I met — I can’t think of his name now — but I started studying with a legitimate bass player from the school, and he had a good sense of humor and whatnot. And I was a little frightened by it. But little by little, okay. The man that really taught me was a gentleman by the name of Homer Mensch. He was a bass player with the New York Philharmonic. And he was like six foot three, big long hands, and…

items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Yes. And I’ve got to tell you this story.

ctx.x: Chubby Jackson was on the band then?

Yes. And I’ve got to tell you this story. We premiered with Walter Hendl, the conductor, pianist and associate conductor with the New York Philharmonic. They still have Stravinsky month at the New York Philharmonic every year. And he had Mickey Fullins playing bass clarinet, which was tom-tom [scats] one strain, and Micky Fullins and Chubby is playing arco, and he doesn’t arco.
He’s not a bow man, right.
